51578990.protein: NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 3
51578990.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to LRR domain of NLRP3 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC Assay: 4.2.9. ITC Assay. The PYD, NACHT, and LRR domains were concentrated with a 10 kDa ultrafiltration tube to obtain higher concentrations of protein. Then, dialysis was performed with a 3.5 kDa dialysis membrane at 4 °C overnight to collect protein and dialysis solution. Protein was diluted with a dialysis tail solution, and DMSO was added to obtain a 20 μM protein solution (containing 5% DMSO). Similarly, compounds were diluted with a dialysis tail solution in different concentrations, and DMSO was regulated to 5%, including 200, 500, 700, 900, and 1200 μM. A 280 μL protein solution was maintained in the sample cell, and the reference cell contained double-distilled water. The dialysis tail containing 5% DMSO was used as the control solution for the protein. A small molecule compound solution was introduced into the sample cell by means of syringes via 19 individual injections at 25 °C, and the amount of each injection was 2 μL. The individual injections were programmed at intervals of 120 s. All the solutions used for ITC experiments were thoroughly degassed prior to use. After the peak area was integrated and the heats of dilution were subtracted, the thermogram for binding was obtained. The titration data were fitted to one set of site models using MicroCal PEAQ-ITC Analysis Software.
original_paragraph.Figure 11 caption: Figure 11. Compounds I-19 and II-8 inhibit the NLRP3-NEK7 interaction by targeting the LRR domain of the NLRP3 protein. The effect of compound I-19 on the NLRP3-NEK7 interaction was analyzed by co-IP (A). ITC titration curve of I-19 (B) and II-8 (C) interaction with the LRR domain. The association and dissociation curves of I-19 with LRR (E), PYD (F), and NACHT (G) domains were detected by BLI (D).
original_paragraph.Figure 11 - ITC Thermograms and Binding: Figure 11B: ITC titration curve of I-19 with LRR domain. The thermogram shows 19 injections of compound I-19 into the LRR domain solution. The binding isotherm (lower panel) shows a sigmoidal curve with a Kd value of 6.41 μM. Figure 11C: ITC titration curve of II-8 with LRR domain. The thermogram shows 19 injections of compound II-8 into the LRR domain solution. The binding isotherm (lower panel) shows a sigmoidal curve with a Kd value of 6.11 μM.
original_paragraph.Figure 11 - BLI Kinetics Table: Table in Figure 11D: Kinetics of the interaction between the domains and Compound I-19. The table lists the following values for the LRR domain: Kd = 1.609 μM, Kon = 4.293x10^4 M/s, Koff = 6.906x10^-2 s^-1. For the NACHT domain: Kd = 88.12 μM, Kon = 6.287x10^3 M/s, Koff = 5.540x10^-1 s^-1. The PYD domain has no data listed.
original_paragraph.Results Section - ITC Results: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), biolayer interferometry (BLI), and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays were employed to investigate the interaction between compounds I-19 and II-8 with NLRP3 protein. The ITC results showed that the binding affinity of the two compounds with the LRR domain is approximately 6 μM (Figure 11B,C). In BLI experiments, the association constant (Kon), dissociation constant (Koff), and equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd = Koff/Kon) were calculated based on the signals. Compound I-19 exhibited the strongest affinity with the LRR domain (Kd = 1.609 μM), weaker affinity with the NACHT domain (Kd = 88.12 μM), and almost no affinity with the PYD domain (Figure 11D–G). The BLI and ITC affinity results for compound I-19 were consistent, both within the same order of magnitude. In summary, these compounds primarily bind to the LRR domain of the NLRP3 protein, with minimal binding to the NACHT and PYD domains. These findings align with the initial design strategy of targeting compounds using the pocket formed by the interaction between the NLRP3-LRR domain and NEK7.
